TERMINAL: a decorator on ToolLoopExecutor.run (modules/tools/execution/reply_chips_turn.py ends_on_reply_chips) wraps the caller's on_tool_result and on_round_end; after a round in which the tool succeeded (called directly, or as platform_execute's action), on_round_end returns ToolPostResult(force_final=True, final_content=<the round's own text, from the assistant message the loop just appended>), and _force_synthesize answers with no model call (tool_loop.py:343-359). The result's response carries reply_chips. A round with no text is not ended early (the loop goes on as today: one more model call writes the answer, and the chips still ride it). A turn that called platform_get_brief is never ended early and carries no chips ('never on the brief'). acceptanceCriteria: modules/tools/execution/reply_chips_turn.py: a decorator ends_on_reply_chips on ToolLoopExecutor.run, stacked beside @answers_at_the_cap. run and _execute_round are byte-identical (K4); tool_loop.py (812 lines) does not grow: move at least the decorator's and its import's lines out (K3) → DONE — orchestrator/modules/tools/execution/reply_chips_turn.py ends_on_reply_chips, stacked between @its_answer_is_checked and @answers_at_the_cap (test_the_terminal_turn_is_a_decorator_on_run walks the chain). ToolLoopExecutor.run and _execute_round are byte-identical (gate N15a, N15b). tool_loop.py 812 -> 810 lines: the decorator and its import in, F099's UNRUN_SOURCE_NOTICE moved out to nudges.py and re-exported (consumers/chatbot/service.py and test_f099 import it from tool_loop). Commit a52cac3ad

It wraps the caller's on_tool_result and on_round_end: after a round in which platform_offer_replies succeeded (called directly, or as platform_execute's action), on_round_end returns ToolPostResult(force_final=True, final_content=<the round's own text, from the assistant message the loop just appended>), so the run answers with no model call. The result's response carries reply_chips (the tool's replies). A caller hook's own force_final still wins → DONE — _ChipsRun wraps both hooks for one run. on_tool_result notes the replies of a call whose action is platform_offer_replies (direct, or platform_execute's action, stripped as the executor strips it) and whose answer succeeded (the chat's raw_result, or the bare answer), checked again with handlers_replies.replies_refusal, then hands the call to the caller's hook unchanged. on_round_end calls the caller's hook first (its force_final wins), then returns ToolPostResult(force_final=True, final_content=round_text(messages)): the last assistant message carrying tool_calls, as written. _force_synthesize makes no model call. The answer carries reply_chips through a new LLMResponse.reply_chips field (core/llm/clients/base.py), so a dataclasses.replace copy (claim_removed.in_place_of) keeps it; a SimpleNamespace is copied with the attribute set. Two changes beyond the AC came from the security review. (1) This early end is NOT marked forced_final: the loop sets the flag and the decorator clears it for its own end only, because the chat's F187 (invented ids) and F205 (internal words) checks skip forced results, and this text is the model's own answer. (2) A caller hook that ends the run on its own words (final_content set: the chat's fatal-error line, or Composio's early return) gets no chips; one that asks the model for the answer (final_content None) does. Commit a52cac3ad

A round with no text is not ended early (the loop goes on as today, and the chips still ride the response it ends with). A run that called platform_get_brief (directly or through platform_execute) is never ended early and carries no chips. A refused platform_offer_replies changes nothing → DONE — An empty or whitespace-only round returns the caller's post, so the loop calls the model again and the chips ride that answer. Both reviews flagged stale chips, and K12 says 'one more model call writes the answer, and the chips still ride it'. So a later round of other work, a refused re-offer included, leaves the earlier chips off, and a later successful offer replaces them. brief_called reads the tracker's outcomes for the whole turn and compares the action stripped: the security review found that ' platform_get_brief' sent through platform_execute ran the brief but was recorded unstripped. A brief turn is never ended early and carries no chips. A refused call (success False) notes nothing. Commit a52cac3ad

New test orchestrator/tests/test_prd268w3_reply_chips_terminal.py, with a fake model that counts its calls: a first response with text and a platform_offer_replies call ends after exactly one model call, its response the round's text with reply_chips; the same through platform_execute; an empty-text round calls the model again; a get_brief turn is not ended and has no chips; a refused call continues the loop; a caller's force_final wins; a run without the tool is unchanged → DONE — orchestrator/tests/test_prd268w3_reply_chips_terminal.py (new). Its fake model counts every call, the turn's first response included. Tests: test_text_and_chips_end_the_run_after_one_model_call (direct and platform_execute, with the chat's envelope and with a bare answer: 1 call, the round's text, reply_chips, not forced), test_the_chips_are_the_tools_replies_as_it_shows_them, test_chips_with_other_calls_in_the_same_round_still_end_it, test_a_round_with_no_text_calls_the_model_again_and_the_chips_ride_its_answer, test_a_round_of_whitespace_is_a_round_with_no_text, test_a_later_round_of_other_work_ends_on_an_answer_without_the_chips, test_a_later_round_that_offers_again_ends_on_its_own_chips, test_a_turn_that_called_the_brief_is_not_ended_early_and_carries_no_chips (direct, platform_execute, a leading space, a trailing newline), test_a_brief_from_an_earlier_round_still_keeps_the_chips_off, test_a_refused_offer_changes_nothing (one, four, a duplicate, too long), test_a_refused_offer_in_a_later_round_offers_nothing_new, test_a_callers_round_end_force_final_wins, test_a_callers_round_end_synthesis_wins_and_calls_the_model, test_a_callers_tool_result_force_final_wins, test_the_claim_check_still_reads_the_rounds_text_and_the_chips_survive_it, test_the_callers_hooks_see_every_call_and_round_as_before, test_a_run_without_the_tool_is_unchanged, test_an_agent_run_with_no_hooks_without_the_tool_is_unchanged, test_a_first_reply_with_no_call_is_unchanged, test_the_terminal_turn_is_a_decorator_on_run, test_the_names_are_the_handlers, test_a_copy_of_the_response_keeps_its_chips, test_a_response_that_cannot_carry_chips_is_sent_as_it_was. Not run with pytest here; CI runs it. It was exercised with python3 against the real loop and handler under a stub-import harness (permissive stubs for the missing third-party packages): 32/32 pass. With the decorator replaced by the identity, 13 fail. With the old unstripped brief check, the two whitespace cases fail. 21 existing tool-loop test files that load under the harness give identical results with and without the decorator. Foreground reviews: code-reviewer and security-reviewer, no CRITICAL or HIGH. Fixed from them: the brief whitespace bypass (M1), the forced flag skipping F187 and F205 (M2), stale chips after a later round, and chips under a caller's own words. Flags for US-C12c, not changed here (service.py is untouched): the chat's F187 and F205 re-prompts and its max-iterations synthesis replace the response, so a re-written answer carries no chips; the round's text was streamed live as narration and is sent again as the final text (K13: the wire carries it once). Flag for US-W03a and US-C12c: a tapped chip is sent as the person's own words, so it must never satisfy a click gate or an approval. Commit a52cac3ad

userStories.title: The turn's parts: reply_chips@1 and follow_up@1 on the saved reply, live in one frame, the text once
userStories.description: As a person, I want the chips, and the follow-up Auto just scheduled, to stay with Auto's reply after a reload, and to appear as the reply finishes (PRD-268 §6.3 'In the thread', §6.6 'Storage', K13).
acceptanceCriteria: consumers/chatbot/turn_parts.py builds the turn's parts once the loop has ended: {type 'reply_chips@1', replies} from the final response's reply_chips, and {type 'follow_up@1', follow_up_id, at} for each successful platform_schedule_follow_up in the turn's tracker (directly or through platform_execute). A turn that called platform_get_brief has no reply_chips@1 → DONE — orchestrator/consumers/chatbot/turn_parts.py (new): turn_parts(final, tracker) gives {type 'reply_chips@1', replies} from the final response's reply_chips, held again to handlers_replies.replies_refusal (chips_part), then {type 'follow_up@1', follow_up_id, at} for each platform_schedule_follow_up the tracker recorded as succeeded, directly or through platform_execute (the action stripped): its row id (a positive whole number) and its time in UTC (a time with no offset gives no part), never its reason. Beyond the AC (security review): a follow-up that a platform_cancel_follow_up of the same turn cancelled gives no part, and each id is one part. A turn whose tracker holds platform_get_brief (stripped, reply_chips_turn.brief_in) gets no reply_chips@1. reply_chips_turn.py exposes action_answer and brief_in (a rename and a split, no change in behaviour) (commit c6ade0986)

The receipts decorators carry them (K4, K13): writes_its_receipts resets the turn's value; the_loop_writes_receipts sets it from the final chunk and yields one tool-data frame under 'turn_parts' before the answer; saves_the_turns_receipts appends the parts after the text part. consumers/chatbot/service.py is untouched → DONE — consumers/chatbot/receipts.py: a _PARTS context variable, reset with the turn's other values in writes_its_receipts; the_loop_writes_receipts sets it from the final chunk (turn_parts of the answer and the loop's own tracker); _frames_once sends turn_parts_frames after the receipts frames: one tool-data frame {turn_parts: [parts]}, once per turn, none for a widget visitor (F155) and none for a turn with no parts; saves_the_turns_receipts appends the parts after the text part, inside a chat turn only. consumers/chatbot/service.py is untouched (gate N16) (commit c6ade0986)

The saved reply holds the round's text exactly once, as its text part; no narration part repeats it, and the wire carries it once. A spoken turn saves its chips, and its text never contains them. A turn with no chips and no follow-up saves exactly today's parts. History (GET the chat's messages, api/chat.py get_chat_messages) returns the parts unchanged → DONE — Before: a round whose chips ended the run streamed its text, its narration frame moved it to the activity trail, service.py's tail streamed it again (the answer was a non-streamed copy) and split_reply saved it as narration and as text. Now on_screen.Screen notes a round that calls platform_offer_replies (turn_parts.offers_replies), and the turn's streams hold its narration frame when it passes them, in stream order: keeps_one_answer_on_screen for the first reply, settles_held_retractions in the loop (the loop runs in its own task, ahead of its frames, so the Screen only notes the round and the stream holds the frame). When the loop's answer is that round's own text (turn_parts.is_its_round: it carries chips and its words are the round's), the frame never goes out and the answer is a copy marked streamed (turn_parts.as_streamed), so service.py sends no tail; narration.split_reply leaves that round out of the narration. Every other path sends the held frame first, as it was: the next text on the stream, any other answer (a refused offer, a brief turn, an F205 or F187 re-prompt, the max-iterations synthesis, the error final) and a loop that ends with no answer; a retracted round's frame never; an answer that cannot be marked keeps its round as narration. A spoken turn saves its chips and its text is the round's alone (the voice speaks text frames only). A turn with no chips and no follow-up saves exactly today's parts. get_chat_messages returns msg.parts unchanged (no code change). Plain and tool turns are unchanged: 16 related test files (FX-017's screen, F186, PRD-256 receipts and honesty, F108, F187, F205, F261, F295, US-C12b) give identical results under the stub harness with and without this change (commit c6ade0986)

New test orchestrator/tests/test_prd268w3_turn_parts.py: driving the receipts decorators with a fake loop, a chips turn saves [receipts, text, reply_chips@1] and sends the turn_parts frame once before the finish; a scheduling turn saves follow_up@1; a get_brief turn saves no chips; the text is saved once and no narration part repeats it; a spoken turn; a plain turn's parts are exactly as before; a widget visitor's turn sends no frame (F155) → DONE — orchestrator/tests/test_prd268w3_turn_parts.py (new, 30 test functions, 40 cases). A turn is driven through writes_its_receipts and keeps_one_answer_on_screen over the real StreamingChatService._stream_tool_loop and a scripted provider streaming through in_owner_words; service.py's first-reply and tail steps are taken as service.py takes them (pinned by test_service_py_takes_the_steps_this_turn_drives), and the frames are applied with the frontend's rule, ported. Tests: a chips turn saves [receipts, text, reply_chips@1] and sends one turn_parts frame after the receipts and before the finish, with one model call; the round's text is on the screen, sent and saved once, with no narration part; chips in a later round; a refused offer (its narration goes out before the next text); a get_brief turn saves no chips; a scheduling turn saves follow_up@1 without the reason; chips and a follow-up together; a refused schedule; a plain turn's parts exactly as before; a tool turn with neither; the next turn starts with no parts; a spoken turn; a widget visitor's turn sends no frame (F155); history returns the parts unchanged; the parts are never read as the reply; the builders (cancelled, duplicate, UTC, a malformed id or time, chips that fail the check, the brief with whitespace), split_reply, offers_replies, the Screen's hold, a retracted held round, a loop with no answer, an answer that cannot be marked, as_streamed, the names. Not run with pytest here; CI runs it. Under the stub harness 38 of 40 cases pass; the 2 that import api.chat cannot load there (the existing PRD-256 test that imports it fails the same way), and their logic was exercised by extracting the two functions. With the three seam files at the base, 12 behaviour cases fail. Foreground reviews: code-reviewer and security-reviewer, no CRITICAL or HIGH. Fixed from them: the held frame goes out at the next text and when a loop ends with no answer, words compared spacing aside, the time in UTC, cancelled and duplicate follow-ups. Flags, not built: a tapped chip is sent as the person's own words, so US-W03a must keep it from satisfying any consent gate; the chips call shows as a read receipt ('replies', looked up) (commit c6ade0986)

userStories.title: The person's follow-up routes: list and cancel their own
userStories.description: As a person, I want to see and cancel the follow-ups Auto promised me, from the thread (PRD-268 §6.3 'In the thread', K8, K22).
acceptanceCriteria: A new router orchestrator/api/proactive_follow_ups.py, RouterSpec('api.proactive_follow_ups'), plain def, authenticated and workspace-scoped: GET /api/proactive/follow-ups?chat_id=&status=pending|all gives the caller's own follow-ups (pending by default), each {id, at, reason, status (pending, fired or cancelled), chat_id}; POST /api/proactive/follow-ups/{follow_up_id}/cancel cancels the caller's own pending one through services/proactive/follow_ups.cancel_follow_up, with require_workspace_permission('agents:execute') (K22) → DONE — orchestrator/api/proactive_follow_ups.py (new; RouterSpec('api.proactive_follow_ups') in router_manifest.py, main.py untouched): list_my_follow_ups GET /api/proactive/follow-ups (chat_id UUID, status Literal pending|all, pending by default) and cancel_my_follow_up POST /api/proactive/follow-ups/{follow_up_id}/cancel (follow_up_id 0 < id < 10**18), both plain def on the sync session; the person from resolve_user_pk only, the workspace from ctx; rows {id, at, reason, status, chat_id} from follow_ups.list_follow_ups / FollowUp.to_dict (at now converted to UTC); the cancel goes through follow_ups.cancel_follow_up with require_workspace_permission('agents:execute') (K22, the sweep's class (a)). userStories.title: Eval scorers, the pass bars and the gold-set reader; no gold set can be committed
userStories.description: As the owner, I want every proactive feature measured against a number before it goes live, with the gold data kept off the public repo (PRD-268 §6.7, US-C13, K14).
acceptanceCriteria: A package orchestrator/evals/proactive/: bars.py holds the §6.7 pass bars as constants (triage: recall of 'act today' >= 0.95, precision >= 0.90, every verdict with a reason of at most 120 characters; silence: >= 0.95 of quiet snapshots silent, >= 0.85 of planted ones naming the need, 0 duplicates; reply chips: chips on >= 16 of 20 choice turns within the limits, 0 turns where the chips replace the answer, <= 1 of 10 open questions; spoken: median <= 40 words, none over 80, no markdown, URL, path or id; one brief: exactly one per person per local date; precision (live): started / decided >= 0.40, started and passed review >= 0.30 of decided, a source agent under 0.20 after 20 decisions listed). scoring.py holds one pure scorer per eval, returning the numbers and pass or miss. gold.py reads <eval>.jsonl from config.PROACTIVE_EVAL_GOLD_DIR and refuses an empty setting, a missing directory or one inside the repository, with a clear message → DONE — orchestrator/evals/proactive/{__init__,bars,scoring,gold}.py. bars.py: the §6.7 bars as constants (TRIAGE_MIN_RECALL 0.95, TRIAGE_MIN_PRECISION 0.90, TRIAGE_REASON_MAX_CHARS 120; SILENCE_MIN_QUIET_SILENT 0.95, SILENCE_MIN_PLANTED_NAMED 0.85, SILENCE_MAX_DUPLICATES 0; CHIPS_MIN_ON_CHOICE 16/20, CHIPS_MAX_REPLACED 0, CHIPS_MAX_ON_OPEN 1/10, plus CHIPS_MAX_OUT_OF_LIMITS 0 for §6.7's 'all within the limits'; SPOKEN_MAX_MEDIAN_WORDS 40, SPOKEN_MAX_WORDS 80; BRIEFS_PER_PERSON_PER_DATE 1; PRECISION_MIN_STARTED 0.40, PRECISION_MIN_PASSED_REVIEW 0.30, PRECISION_SLOW_AGENT_SHARE 0.20 after PRECISION_SLOW_AGENT_DECISIONS 20) and BAR_TEXT, each bar in words built from them, for the runners to print. scoring.py: score_triage, score_silence, score_reply_chips, score_spoken, score_one_brief, score_precision, each returning a Score (numbers, PASS or MISS, as_dict for --json); a share with nothing to divide is None and never passes. Chips are within the limits when the tool's own replies_refusal keeps them; a duplicate is a title equal under dedupe's normalise_title to an open or hidden one; a planted need is named when one suggestion's title and detail carry each of its words where a word starts. The chips bars are shares (16/20, 1/10), so a gold set of another size is still scored. gold.py: read_gold(<eval>) reads <eval>.jsonl (triage, silence, reply_chips, spoken; precision and one_brief have none) from config.PROACTIVE_EVAL_GOLD_DIR, raising GoldSetUnavailable (US-C13b's exit 2) for an empty setting, a path that is not a folder, a folder inside the repository (compared by the file system, so a link or another case is still inside; the repository is the nearest folder holding .git, else the orchestrator folder, as in the image), and a missing, unreadable, malformed or empty file. For US-C13b: report_triage answers needs_attention and severity (fyi, worth_a_look, needs_a_decision, urgent) and no reason, so its runner maps those to act_today / can_wait and must source the reason. Commit 96658aec5

userStories.title: Three small hardenings: the follow-up list off the event loop, a bounded cap count under the lock, and calibration's person checked both ways
userStories.description: As the owner, I want the review's three low findings in W3's own code closed in the same fix pass, since each is a few lines (W3 review findings, raised by the code-reviewer, the database-reviewer and the security-reviewer; LOW).
acceptanceCriteria: Cause (a): handlers_follow_ups.list_follow_ups is an async def that calls _listed on the chat turn's session directly, so recipients(), auto_agent_id() and follow_ups.list_follow_ups run their synchronous reads on the event loop. Schedule and cancel already run on a worker thread with a session of their own (_on_own_session through asyncio.to_thread). AGENTS.md says no blocking work on the event loop. Change: list runs _listed the same way, on its own session in a worker thread; its answer is unchanged. Test: the list handler runs _listed through asyncio.to_thread on a session that is not the turn's (patch to_thread or _own_session and assert), and its existing tests still pass.

Cause (b): follow_ups._COUNTS has no bound in its WHERE beyond the workspace and deliver_as. Inside the workspace's advisory lock it visits every follow-up row the workspace ever had, with a heap fetch for status, which the partial index lacks. Rows are never purged, so the scan grows by up to 100 rows a day under a lock every schedule call waits on. Change: its WHERE gains AND (status = 'active' OR created_at > :since). The three numbers are the same (a pending row is at most PROACTIVE_FOLLOW_UP_MAX_DAYS old; the day counts read only the last 24 hours), and the scan is bounded. Keep P268W3-RVW-1's missed rule in the pending count. Test: the statement carries the bound, and a realdb case with fired rows older than 24 hours gives the same counts as before. The existing cap tests, including six at once with a cap of five, still pass.

Cause (c): services/calibration/offer.py _post hands deliver_background_message clerk_user_id=recorded_person(db, user_id) without checking that it resolves back to the same person. follow_up_fire._recorded checks it with core.auth.actor.resolve_recorded_person.
